gates.requirement: CompatibilityTargetManifest pins every ecosystem target by native name, version, revision, contracts, fixture digest, platform, adapter commit, and passed profile.
Imported and projected artifacts retain native identifiers, contract versions, statuses, attribution, uncertainty, units, and times without converting them into QSTE identity.
MASA and Earworm projections validate against byte-frozen external JSON Schemas; a schema rejection creates no derivative.
Cosmoaudition structural validation records that no external JSON Schema is published, and structural validity never silently becomes live interoperability.
Akousmata and Listening Stack remain read-only inspection or metadata routes and make no interoperability claim by association.

Unavailable and required-but-untested capabilities return unavailable/capability_unavailable with unavailable or untested capability status; prohibited targets return refused/policy_refused/prohibited.
Every completed engine fixture records parameters, bounded logs, output digests, return state, and timeout state.
The process demonstration invokes only the packaged QSTE fixture module through an argument array; payload or prompt content cannot provide a command, executable, patch, DSP graph, or network target.
The OSC demonstration binds an ephemeral receiver to 127.0.0.1, preserves sent and received packet digests, and invokes no external engine.
Pure Data, Max/MSP, SuperCollider, and Csound stay unavailable when absent; synthetic fixtures do not upgrade their capability or interoperability status.
Import, projection, inspection, process, loopback, failure, unavailable, and refusal paths produce durable operation receipts and immutable events.

P11 tests and runtime write only inside the caller-owned QSTE workspace and perform no playback, model execution, provider access, public release, participant interaction, or adjacent-checkout mutation.
